A Brief History of Empirical Modeling
Scientific Modeling Principles and Differential Equations

Ethics, Uncertainty, and the Art of Engineering

nodes.name: model
nodes.label: Model
nodes.definition: A simplified representation of some part of reality, chosen to make it graspable and to predict it.

nodes.name: representation
nodes.label: Representation
nodes.definition: Something that stands in for a set of experiences or objects so they can be reasoned about as one thing.

nodes.name: clustering
nodes.label: Clustering
nodes.definition: Grouping unlabeled data points so that points in the same group are more similar to each other than to points in other groups.

nodes.name: abstraction
nodes.label: Abstraction
nodes.definition: Deliberately ignoring details so that many different things can be treated as one; every model is a choice of what to ignore.

nodes.name: extrapolation
nodes.label: Extrapolation
nodes.definition: Using a pattern compressed from past observations to predict cases beyond those observations.

nodes.name: induction
nodes.label: Induction
nodes.definition: Inferring a general rule from repeated specific observations, such as concluding the sun will rise because it always has.

nodes.name: domain of validity
nodes.label: Domain of validity
nodes.definition: The range of conditions under which a model gives useful predictions, beyond which it breaks down.

nodes.name: falsification
nodes.label: Falsification
nodes.definition: Testing a model by actively trying to prove it wrong, since a model can never be proven right.

nodes.name: model refinement
nodes.label: Model refinement
nodes.definition: Replacing a working model with a deeper one that explains it and extends further, as kinetic theory did for temperature.

nodes.name: function approximation
nodes.label: Function approximation
nodes.definition: Finding a function F that maps inputs x to outputs y from examples, the common shape of most machine learning tasks.

nodes.name: supervised learning
nodes.label: Supervised learning
nodes.definition: Learning a mapping from inputs to outputs using examples where the correct output is given.

nodes.name: unsupervised learning
nodes.label: Unsupervised learning
nodes.definition: Finding structure in data that comes without labels, such as clusters or low-dimensional directions.

nodes.name: program
nodes.label: Program
nodes.definition: A precise sequence of instructions that a computer follows exactly, with no common sense to fill gaps.

nodes.name: programming language
nodes.label: Programming language
nodes.definition: A formal language, like Python, in which every statement has exactly one meaning, used to write programs.

nodes.name: arithmetic operator
nodes.label: Arithmetic operator
nodes.definition: A symbol such as +, /, ** or % that computes a number from other numbers in code.

nodes.name: variable
nodes.label: Variable
nodes.definition: A name attached to a value in a program so it can be referred to and reused.

nodes.name: assignment
nodes.label: Assignment
nodes.definition: The action written with = in code: compute the right-hand side, then attach the name on the left to the result.

nodes.name: data type
nodes.label: Data type
nodes.definition: The kind of a value (number, text, boolean) that determines what operations on it mean.

nodes.name: list
nodes.label: List
nodes.definition: An ordered collection of values in a program, accessed by position.

nodes.name: indexing
nodes.label: Indexing
nodes.definition: Retrieving an element of a sequence by its position, counting from zero in Python.

nodes.name: conditional
nodes.label: Conditional
nodes.definition: An if/else statement that runs different code depending on whether a condition is true.

nodes.name: loop
nodes.label: Loop
nodes.definition: A statement that repeats a block of code for each item or until a stopping rule is met.

nodes.name: execution trace
nodes.label: Execution trace
nodes.definition: Following a program line by line while tracking what value each name holds, to see what the computer actually does.

nodes.name: function
nodes.label: Function
nodes.definition: A named, reusable rule that takes inputs and returns an output, both in mathematics and as a recipe in code.

nodes.name: dictionary
nodes.label: Dictionary
nodes.definition: A container that maps keys to values, so a value is found by its key rather than by its position.

nodes.name: debugging
nodes.label: Debugging
nodes.definition: Finding and fixing errors in a program, starting by reading what the error message says.

nodes.name: symbolic ai
nodes.label: Symbolic AI
nodes.definition: The early approach to artificial intelligence that hand-codes rules and searches over symbols, rather than learning from data.

nodes.name: machine learning
nodes.label: Machine learning
nodes.definition: Building systems that learn rules or patterns from data instead of having them programmed by hand.

nodes.name: moores law
nodes.label: Moore's law
nodes.definition: The observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years.

nodes.name: compute scaling
nodes.label: Compute scaling
nodes.definition: The growth by many orders of magnitude of the computation used to train AI systems, a main driver of recent progress.

nodes.name: log scale
nodes.slide: Or Just Ask For the Plot
nodes.label: Log scale
nodes.definition: A plot axis where equal distances mean equal ratios, used when values span many orders of magnitude.

nodes.name: curve fitting
nodes.slide: A Lot of It Is Curve Fitting
nodes.label: Curve fitting
nodes.definition: Choosing a function whose curve passes close to a set of data points.

nodes.name: graph
nodes.label: Graph
nodes.definition: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to represent relationships such as social networks, maps or molecules.

nodes.name: data representation
nodes.label: Data representation
nodes.definition: The way something recorded from the world, like sound, images or text, is turned into numbers a machine can process.

nodes.name: tabular data
nodes.label: Tabular data
nodes.definition: Data arranged as a table, where each row is an example and each column is a measured quantity.

nodes.name: time series
nodes.label: Time series
nodes.definition: A sequence of measurements indexed by time, such as a stock price recorded each day.

nodes.name: audio signal
nodes.label: Audio signal
nodes.definition: Sound recorded as an array of air-pressure samples taken many thousands of times per second.

nodes.name: spectrogram
nodes.slide: From a Wave to a Picture
nodes.label: Spectrogram
nodes.definition: A picture of a sound showing how much energy each frequency has over time, built from short-time Fourier transforms.

nodes.name: fourier transform
nodes.slide: From a Wave to a Picture
nodes.label: Fourier transform
nodes.definition: A transformation that rewrites a signal as a sum of sinusoids, revealing which frequencies it contains.

nodes.name: image representation
nodes.label: Image representation
nodes.definition: An image stored as a grid of pixel values, of shape height by width by number of channels.

nodes.name: color channel
nodes.label: Color channel
nodes.definition: One of the red, green or blue grids of intensities that together make up a colour image.

nodes.name: tensor
nodes.label: Tensor
nodes.definition: A multi-dimensional array of numbers, such as a video of shape time by height by width by channels.

nodes.name: word embedding
nodes.label: Word embedding
nodes.definition: A dense vector for each word, learned so that directions and distances between vectors carry meaning.

nodes.name: adjacency matrix
nodes.label: Adjacency matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix whose entry (i, j) is 1 when node i connects to node j, representing a graph as numbers.

nodes.name: modeling learning inference
nodes.slide: The Three Pillars of Artificial Intelligence
nodes.label: Modeling, learning, inference
nodes.definition: The three pillars of AI: build a simplified model, estimate its parameters from data, then use it to answer questions.

nodes.name: classification
nodes.label: Classification
nodes.definition: Predicting a discrete label, such as fraud or not fraud, from an input.

nodes.name: regression
nodes.label: Regression
nodes.definition: Predicting a continuous numerical value, such as a house price, from an input.

nodes.name: structured prediction
nodes.label: Structured prediction
nodes.definition: Predicting an output with internal structure, such as a sentence or a parse tree, rather than a single label or number.

nodes.name: histogram
nodes.label: Histogram
nodes.definition: A bar chart of how many data samples fall into each range of values.

nodes.name: probability density function
nodes.label: Probability density function
nodes.definition: A curve describing how likely a continuous variable is to take values near each point; a model of the data, unlike the histogram.

nodes.name: notation and code
nodes.label: Notation and code
nodes.definition: Every mathematical idea in the course is written two ways, as compact notation and as runnable code, and each translates directly into the other.

nodes.name: iteration
nodes.slide: The loop that predicts the future
nodes.label: Iteration
nodes.definition: Repeating one update step in a loop, so that a model like next year's population from this year's steps forward through time.

nodes.name: vectors
nodes.label: Vectors
nodes.definition: An ordered list of numbers, pictured as an arrow with direction and length; in machine learning one example, one row of data, is a vector.

nodes.name: inner product
nodes.label: Inner product
nodes.definition: The sum of elementwise products of two vectors, also called the dot product; the single most common operation in machine learning.

nodes.name: norm
nodes.slide: How Long, How Far, How Similar
nodes.label: Norm
nodes.definition: A measure of a vector's length, such as the L2 (Euclidean), L1 (sum of absolute values), or max norm; distances between examples are norms of differences.

nodes.name: cosine similarity
nodes.slide: How Long, How Far, How Similar
nodes.label: Cosine similarity
nodes.definition: The cosine of the angle between two vectors, their dot product divided by both lengths, measuring how similar their directions are regardless of size.

nodes.name: matrix
nodes.label: Matrix
nodes.definition: A rectangular array of numbers with rows and columns; it can hold a whole dataset or act as a linear transformation of vectors.

nodes.name: matrix product
nodes.label: Matrix multiplication
nodes.definition: Combining two matrices so each output entry is a row-by-column dot product; in NumPy it is A @ B, not the elementwise A * B.

nodes.name: linear transformation
nodes.slide: A matrix is a machine that moves space
nodes.label: Linear transformation
nodes.definition: A map that moves space while keeping lines straight and the origin fixed; a matrix's columns record where the basis vectors land.

nodes.name: determinant
nodes.slide: A matrix is a machine that moves space
nodes.label: Determinant
nodes.definition: The factor by which a matrix scales area or volume; a determinant of zero means the matrix flattens space and cannot be inverted.

nodes.name: eigenvector
nodes.slide: A matrix is a machine that moves space
nodes.label: Eigenvector
nodes.definition: A direction that a matrix only stretches or shrinks without turning; the stretch factor is its eigenvalue.

nodes.name: composition
nodes.slide: Two machines in a row are one machine
nodes.label: Composition of transformations
nodes.definition: Applying one linear transformation after another, which equals multiplying their matrices; order matters, so RS generally differs from SR.

nodes.name: column space
nodes.label: Column space
nodes.definition: The set of all outputs Ax, read as weighted sums of the columns of A, where x supplies the weights.

nodes.name: span
nodes.label: Span
nodes.definition: Everything you can build from a set of vectors by scaling and adding them together.

nodes.name: rank
nodes.label: Rank
nodes.definition: The number of linearly independent columns of a matrix, which is the dimension of the space its outputs can reach.

nodes.name: inverse
nodes.slide: Inverse, Determinant, and When Things Break
nodes.label: Matrix inverse
nodes.definition: The matrix that undoes A, so multiplying them gives the identity; it solves the linear system Ax = b when it exists.

nodes.name: condition number
nodes.label: Condition number
nodes.definition: A measure of how much a matrix amplifies small errors when inverted; nearly duplicate columns make it huge and the solution unreliable.

nodes.name: derivative
nodes.slide: A derivative is what a curve looks like up close
nodes.label: Derivative
nodes.definition: The slope of a curve at a point, what the curve looks like up close: how fast the output changes as the input nudges.

nodes.name: integral
nodes.label: Integral
nodes.definition: The accumulated total of a rate, the area under its curve; integration and differentiation undo each other.

nodes.name: gradient
nodes.label: Gradient
nodes.definition: The vector of partial derivatives of a function with respect to each parameter, pointing in the direction of steepest increase.

nodes.name: normal equations
nodes.slide: The One Gradient You Will Use All Semester
nodes.label: Normal equations
nodes.definition: The linear system obtained by setting the least-squares gradient to zero, whose solution gives the best-fit parameters in closed form.

nodes.name: projection
nodes.label: Projection
nodes.definition: The closest point to a vector within a subspace; least squares projects the targets onto the space spanned by the feature columns.

nodes.name: chain rule
nodes.slide: The chain rule, as a picture
nodes.label: Chain rule
nodes.definition: The rule that the derivative of a composition is the product of the derivatives of its parts, which is how networks compute gradients.

nodes.name: backpropagation
nodes.slide: The chain rule, as a picture
nodes.label: Backpropagation
nodes.definition: Computing all gradients of a network efficiently by applying the chain rule backward from the loss through each operation.

nodes.name: aliasing
nodes.slide: A variable is a label, not a box
nodes.label: Variable aliasing
nodes.definition: A Python variable is a label on an object, not a box, so two names can share one object and a change through either shows in both.

nodes.name: broadcasting
nodes.slide: Broadcasting, and the Bug It Causes
nodes.label: Broadcasting
nodes.definition: NumPy's rule for combining arrays of different shapes by stretching size-one dimensions, a convenience that also causes silent shape bugs.

nodes.name: vectorization
nodes.slide: Avoid Loops if You Can! Vectorize.
nodes.label: Vectorization
nodes.definition: Replacing explicit Python loops with whole-array operations, which run in optimized compiled code and are often hundreds of times faster.

nodes.name: dataframe
nodes.label: DataFrame
nodes.definition: A pandas table of labeled columns used to read, inspect, summarize, and clean a dataset before turning it into numeric arrays.

nodes.name: design matrix
nodes.label: Design matrix
nodes.definition: The data matrix with one row per example and one column per feature, with the target held in a separate vector.

nodes.name: correlation
nodes.label: Correlation
nodes.definition: A number between minus one and one measuring how linearly two variables move together, the dot product of their standardized columns divided by their count.

nodes.name: missing variable
nodes.label: Missing variable (Simpson's paradox)
nodes.definition: A trend in pooled data can reverse within groups when a hidden variable, such as species, drives both measurements.

nodes.name: dataset
nodes.label: Dataset
nodes.definition: A table of examples and measurements that you can visualize, summarize, clean, and use to make predictions.

nodes.name: feature
nodes.label: Feature
nodes.definition: An input variable given to the model, such as a house's size, bedrooms, or age.

nodes.name: target
nodes.label: Target
nodes.definition: The output variable the model is trying to predict, also called the label, such as a house's price.

nodes.name: training example
nodes.wiki: Training, validation, and test data sets
nodes.label: Training example
nodes.definition: One input and output pair from the data, indexed by i, used to fit the model.

nodes.name: hypothesis
nodes.label: Hypothesis
nodes.definition: The function a learning algorithm chooses to map inputs to predicted outputs.

nodes.name: parameters
nodes.label: Parameters
nodes.definition: The numbers, often called theta, that select one specific function from within the chosen model class and are adjusted by training.

nodes.name: model class
nodes.label: Model class
nodes.definition: The family of candidate functions a learner searches over, such as linear, polynomial, or neural network models.

nodes.name: linear model
nodes.label: Linear model
nodes.definition: A prediction that is a weighted sum of the features plus an intercept, written as a single inner product of parameters and inputs.

nodes.name: intercept
nodes.label: Intercept
nodes.definition: The constant term of a linear model, handled by adding a feature that is always one; it is the prediction when all features are zero.

nodes.name: residual
nodes.label: Residual
nodes.definition: The difference between a model's prediction and the actual target for one example.

nodes.name: cost function
nodes.label: Cost function
nodes.definition: A single number measuring how badly the model fits the data, such as half the sum of squared residuals, which training tries to minimize.

nodes.name: loss landscape
nodes.label: Loss landscape
nodes.definition: The surface formed by the cost at every possible parameter setting; its lowest point is the best fit.

nodes.name: gradient descent
nodes.label: Gradient descent
nodes.definition: An optimization method that repeatedly steps the parameters a small amount opposite the gradient, walking downhill on the cost.

nodes.name: learning rate
nodes.label: Learning rate
nodes.definition: The step size in gradient descent; too small is slow, too large overshoots and can diverge.

nodes.name: lms rule
nodes.label: LMS update rule
nodes.definition: The least-mean-squares gradient step for linear regression, which moves each parameter in proportion to the prediction error times its feature.

nodes.name: sgd
nodes.label: Stochastic gradient descent
nodes.definition: Gradient descent that updates the parameters using one randomly chosen example (or small batch) per step, giving a faster but noisier path.

nodes.name: centering
nodes.slide: Why we measure from the average house
nodes.label: Centering features
nodes.definition: Subtracting a feature's mean so the intercept describes a typical example, which decouples slope and intercept and speeds up gradient descent.

nodes.name: multiple regression
nodes.label: Multiple regression
nodes.definition: Linear regression with several features at once, where each coefficient's value depends on which other features are included.

nodes.name: holding fixed
nodes.slide: θj answers one question at a time
nodes.label: Holding other variables fixed
nodes.definition: A regression coefficient is the change in prediction per unit of its feature with every other feature held fixed, so it depends on the company it keeps.

nodes.name: gaussian noise
nodes.slide: Why Least Squares? A Probabilistic View
nodes.label: Gaussian noise model
nodes.definition: The assumption that each target equals the model's prediction plus independent, normally distributed noise with mean zero.

nodes.name: likelihood
nodes.label: Likelihood
nodes.definition: The probability of the observed data viewed as a function of the parameters; for independent examples it is a product over them.

nodes.name: maximum likelihood
nodes.label: Maximum likelihood estimation
nodes.definition: Choosing parameters that make the observed data most probable; with Gaussian noise this is exactly least squares.

nodes.name: outlier
nodes.label: Outlier
nodes.definition: An unusual data point far from the pattern; squared error lets it pull the fit strongly toward itself.

nodes.name: l1 loss
nodes.label: Absolute error (L1 loss)
nodes.definition: A cost that sums absolute residuals instead of squared ones, which corresponds to Laplacian noise and is less sensitive to outliers.

nodes.name: k nearest neighbours
nodes.slide: Given a new input, what’s the output?
nodes.label: k-nearest neighbours
nodes.definition: Predicting the output for a new input by averaging the outputs of the k training examples closest to it.

nodes.name: hypothesis choice
nodes.slide: How do you choose the hypothesis?
nodes.label: Choosing the hypothesis
nodes.definition: The same data admits many fitting functions, so deciding which family of functions to use is a central modeling choice.

nodes.name: feature map
nodes.label: Feature map
nodes.definition: A transformation that builds new features from raw inputs, such as Galton's mid-parent height or polynomial powers of x, before fitting a model.

nodes.name: regression to the mean
nodes.label: Regression to the mean
nodes.definition: Galton's finding that children of unusually tall or short parents tend to be closer to average, which gave regression its name.

nodes.name: r squared
nodes.slide: A Fifth of the Variance, and a Whole Discipline
nodes.label: R squared
nodes.definition: The fraction of the target's variance explained by a fit: one minus residual variation over total variation.

nodes.name: overfitting
nodes.slide: How to choose φ(x)? How to optimize over φ(x)
nodes.label: Overfitting
nodes.definition: When a model is too flexible and fits noise in the training data, giving low training error but poor performance on new data (high variance).

nodes.name: underfitting
nodes.slide: How to choose φ(x)? How to optimize over φ(x)
nodes.label: Underfitting
nodes.definition: When a model is too simple to capture the real pattern, giving high error even on the training data (high bias).

nodes.name: generalization
nodes.slide: How can we tell if φ(·) is good?
nodes.label: Generalization
nodes.definition: A model's ability to perform well on new, unseen data, which is the real goal of machine learning.

nodes.name: test set
nodes.slide: How can we tell if φ(·) is good?
nodes.wiki: Training, validation, and test data sets
nodes.label: Test set
nodes.definition: Data held out from training and used once at the end to estimate how well the model generalizes.

nodes.name: bias variance
nodes.label: Bias-variance trade-off
nodes.definition: As model complexity grows, error from too-simple assumptions (bias) falls while error from sensitivity to the particular data (variance) rises.

nodes.name: hyperparameter
nodes.label: Hyperparameter
nodes.definition: A setting chosen outside the training loop, such as the number of epochs, the step size, or the feature map.

nodes.name: validation set
nodes.slide: Optimize over φ and other hyperparameters
nodes.wiki: Training, validation, and test data sets
nodes.label: Validation set
nodes.definition: Held-out data used during development to compare models and tune hyperparameters, kept separate from the final test set.

nodes.name: cross validation
nodes.slide: Cross validation: every house takes a turn being new
nodes.label: Cross-validation
nodes.definition: Splitting data into folds and letting each fold take a turn as the validation set, averaging the results for a more reliable estimate.

nodes.name: regularization
nodes.label: Regularization
nodes.definition: Adding a penalty on parameter size to the cost, weighted by lambda, to shrink the hypothesis class and reduce overfitting.

nodes.name: l2 regularization
nodes.label: L2 regularization
nodes.definition: A penalty on the squared size of the parameters (ridge) that shrinks all coefficients smoothly toward zero.

nodes.name: l1 regularization
nodes.label: L1 regularization
nodes.definition: A penalty on the sum of absolute parameter values (lasso) that tends to drive some coefficients exactly to zero.

nodes.name: sigmoid
nodes.slide: What if y is a label?
nodes.label: Sigmoid
nodes.definition: The logistic function 1/(1+e^-z), which squashes any real score into a probability between 0 and 1.

nodes.name: logistic regression
nodes.slide: What if y is a label?
nodes.label: Logistic regression
nodes.definition: A classifier that passes a linear score through the sigmoid function to output the probability that the label is one.

nodes.name: negative log likelihood
nodes.label: Negative log-likelihood
nodes.definition: The negative logarithm of the likelihood, averaged over examples, used as a loss to minimise.

nodes.name: convexity
nodes.label: Convexity
nodes.definition: A property of a function shaped like a bowl, so that any local minimum is the global minimum.

nodes.name: cross entropy
nodes.label: Cross-entropy loss
nodes.definition: The loss for predicted probabilities that is near zero when confident and right and grows without bound when confident and wrong.

nodes.name: decision boundary
nodes.label: Decision boundary
nodes.definition: The surface in input space where a classifier switches its prediction from one class to another.

nodes.name: margin
nodes.label: Margin
nodes.definition: The signed distance of a point from the decision boundary, positive when it is classified correctly.

nodes.name: confusion matrix
nodes.slide: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?
nodes.label: Confusion matrix
nodes.definition: A table counting true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives of a classifier.

nodes.name: precision and recall
nodes.slide: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?
nodes.label: Precision and recall
nodes.definition: Precision is the fraction of flagged cases that are real; recall is the fraction of real cases that were flagged.

nodes.name: accuracy
nodes.slide: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?
nodes.label: Accuracy
nodes.definition: The fraction of all predictions that are correct, which can mislead when classes are imbalanced.

nodes.name: f1 score
nodes.slide: The Same Four Numbers on One Screening
nodes.label: F1 score
nodes.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number that is low if either one is low.

nodes.name: class imbalance
nodes.label: Class imbalance
nodes.definition: When one class is much rarer than the others, so that always predicting the majority class looks accurate.

nodes.name: classification threshold
nodes.label: Classification threshold
nodes.definition: The probability cutoff above which a classifier predicts the positive class, chosen after training to trade precision against recall.

nodes.name: multiclass classification
nodes.label: Multiclass classification
nodes.definition: Classification where the label can take one of more than two values.

nodes.name: one vs all
nodes.slide: How to turn scores into probabilities?Note: this slide explains the intuition. Softmax regression is not exactly equivalent to a combination of one-vs-all classifiers.
nodes.label: One-vs-all
nodes.definition: Handling many classes by training one binary classifier per class against all the others.

nodes.name: softmax
nodes.slide: How to turn scores into probabilities?
nodes.label: Softmax
nodes.definition: A function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities by exponentiating and normalising them.

nodes.name: softmax regression
nodes.slide: How to turn scores into probabilities?
nodes.label: Softmax regression
nodes.definition: The generalisation of logistic regression to many classes, with one linear score per class passed through softmax.

nodes.name: logit
nodes.label: Logit
nodes.definition: The raw score of a class before it is turned into a probability by a sigmoid or softmax.

nodes.name: bernoulli
nodes.label: Bernoulli distribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of a single yes or no outcome, equal to one with probability p and zero with probability one minus p.

nodes.name: exponential family
nodes.label: Exponential family
nodes.definition: A broad class of distributions, including Gaussian, Bernoulli, and Poisson, sharing one form that yields the same learning update rule.

nodes.name: natural parameter
nodes.label: Natural parameter
nodes.definition: The parameter eta of an exponential-family distribution that multiplies the outcome inside the exponential; in a GLM it equals the linear score of the inputs.

nodes.name: log partition function
nodes.label: Log partition function
nodes.definition: The term in an exponential-family distribution that normalizes probabilities to sum to one; its derivatives give the mean and variance.

nodes.name: poisson distribution
nodes.label: Poisson distribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of the number of independent events in a fixed window, such as earthquakes in a decade, governed by an average rate.

nodes.name: poisson regression
nodes.slide: How many earthquakes of each size?
nodes.label: Poisson regression
nodes.definition: A generalized linear model for count data where the logarithm of the expected count is linear in the features.

nodes.name: generalized linear model
nodes.label: Generalized linear model
nodes.definition: A model that passes a linear score of the inputs through a response function matched to an exponential-family output, with the same training loop.

nodes.name: link function
nodes.label: Link function
nodes.definition: The function connecting a GLM's expected output to its linear score; its inverse, the response function, turns the score into a prediction.

nodes.name: one hot
nodes.label: One-hot encoding
nodes.definition: Representing each item of a fixed vocabulary as a vector of zeros with a single one in its own position.

nodes.name: bag of words
nodes.label: Bag of words
nodes.definition: Representing a document by which vocabulary words it contains, ignoring their order.

nodes.name: class conditional
nodes.label: Class-conditional probability
nodes.definition: The probability of a feature given the class label, such as how often the word free appears in spam.

nodes.name: naive bayes assumption
nodes.label: Naive Bayes assumption
nodes.definition: The simplifying assumption that features are conditionally independent given the label, so a message's probability is a product over its words.

nodes.name: bayes rule
nodes.label: Bayes' rule
nodes.definition: A formula that reverses conditional probabilities, getting the probability of a label given the data from the probability of the data given the label and the prior.

nodes.name: prior
nodes.label: Prior
nodes.definition: The probability of a class before seeing any features, such as how common spam is overall.

nodes.name: naive bayes
nodes.label: Naive Bayes classifier
nodes.definition: A classifier that estimates class priors and per-feature class-conditional probabilities by counting, then combines them with Bayes' rule.

nodes.name: laplace smoothing
nodes.label: Laplace smoothing
nodes.definition: Adding a small count to every word and class so that an unseen word does not get probability zero and wipe out the whole product.

nodes.name: event model
nodes.slide: Two ways to generate an email
nodes.label: Event model
nodes.definition: The assumed story of how a message is generated, either a coin flip per vocabulary word (multivariate Bernoulli) or words drawn one at a time (multinomial).

nodes.name: generative model
nodes.label: Generative model
nodes.definition: A model that learns how each class's data is distributed, plus the class priors, then classifies with Bayes' rule and can generate new examples.

nodes.name: discriminative model
nodes.label: Discriminative model
nodes.definition: A model that learns the probability of the label given the input directly, drawing the decision boundary without modeling the inputs.

nodes.name: multivariate gaussian
nodes.label: Multivariate Gaussian
nodes.definition: The bell-shaped distribution over vectors, described by a mean vector and a covariance matrix that sets its spreads and correlations.

nodes.name: covariance
nodes.label: Covariance matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix whose diagonal holds each variable's variance and whose off-diagonal entries measure how pairs of variables vary together.

nodes.name: gda
nodes.label: Gaussian discriminant analysis
nodes.definition: A generative classifier that models each class's features as a multivariate Gaussian and classifies new points using Bayes' rule.

nodes.name: language model
nodes.label: Language model
nodes.definition: A model that assigns probabilities to text by predicting each next word from the words before it.

nodes.name: n gram
nodes.label: n-gram model
nodes.definition: A language model that predicts the next word from only the previous few words, estimated by counting word sequences.

nodes.name: threshold unit
nodes.label: Threshold unit (McCulloch-Pitts neuron)
nodes.definition: An artificial neuron that outputs one when a weighted sum of its inputs reaches a threshold and zero otherwise, enough to build logic gates.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.label: Layer
nodes.definition: A set of units computed together, where each output is a weighted sum of all inputs, so the whole layer is one matrix times the input vector.

nodes.name: activation function
nodes.label: Activation function
nodes.definition: A nonlinear function applied after each linear step in a network; without it, stacked layers collapse into a single linear map.

nodes.name: relu
nodes.label: ReLU
nodes.definition: The rectified linear unit activation, which outputs its input when positive and zero otherwise.

nodes.name: neural network
nodes.label: Neural network
nodes.definition: A model built by alternating linear maps and nonlinear activations, learning its own features in hidden layers.

nodes.name: hidden layer
nodes.label: Hidden layer
nodes.definition: An intermediate layer between input and output whose activations are features the network learns for itself.

nodes.name: deep network
nodes.label: Deep network
nodes.definition: A neural network with many stacked hidden layers, each building features from the layer before it.

nodes.name: universal approximation
nodes.slide: How Expressive Is One Hidden Layer?
nodes.label: Universal approximation
nodes.definition: The theorem that one hidden layer with enough neurons and a non-polynomial activation can approximate any continuous function on a bounded domain.

nodes.name: convolution
nodes.label: Convolution
nodes.definition: Sliding one small set of shared weights (a kernel) across an image so the same pattern is detected wherever it appears.

nodes.name: autoencoder
nodes.label: Autoencoder
nodes.definition: A network trained to reproduce its input through a narrow bottleneck, learning a compressed representation with an encoder and decoder.

nodes.name: recurrent network
nodes.label: Recurrent neural network
nodes.definition: A network that processes sequences step by step, carrying a hidden state that acts as memory from one step to the next.

nodes.name: computation graph
nodes.label: Computation graph
nodes.definition: A representation of a formula as a graph of small operations, each knowing its local derivatives, which makes automatic backpropagation possible.

nodes.name: superposition
nodes.label: Superposition
nodes.definition: In a linear system, the response to a sum of inputs is the sum of the responses, so a problem can be split into parts and the solutions added.

nodes.name: nonlinearity
nodes.label: Nonlinearity
nodes.definition: A system is nonlinear when its response is not proportional to its input, so superposition fails and closed-form solutions are usually out of reach.

nodes.name: numerical simulation
nodes.label: Numerical simulation
nodes.definition: Computing an approximate solution of a model, typically a differential equation, step by step on a computer instead of solving it on paper.

nodes.name: scientific modeling cycle
nodes.label: Scientific modeling cycle
nodes.definition: The loop of deriving equations, building a solver, simulating, comparing predictions with observations, and refining the model.

nodes.name: empirical law
nodes.label: Empirical law
nodes.definition: A law found by measuring how a controlled input changes an output, usually a simple proportionality whose constant gets a physical meaning, like Hooke's or Ohm's law.

nodes.name: least squares
nodes.label: Least squares
nodes.definition: Fitting a model by choosing parameters that minimise the sum of squared differences between predictions and data, developed by Legendre and Gauss.

nodes.name: compression reconstruction
nodes.slide: From the World to a Model, and Back
nodes.label: Compression and reconstruction
nodes.definition: Learning compresses many observations into a compact model, and inference reconstructs high-dimensional predictions from that model.

nodes.name: equation discovery
nodes.slide: The Same Three Pillars, for a Field
nodes.label: Equation discovery
nodes.definition: Learning the parameters or terms of a differential equation by fitting it to measured time derivatives of a field.

nodes.name: data pipeline
nodes.slide: The Data Science Hierarchy of Needs
nodes.label: Data pipeline
nodes.definition: The infrastructure that collects, stores, moves, cleans and labels data before any model is trained on it.

nodes.name: nyquist frequency
nodes.slide: From a Wave to a Picture
nodes.label: Nyquist frequency
nodes.definition: Half the sampling rate, the highest frequency a sampled signal can represent.

nodes.name: generative adversarial network
nodes.label: Generative adversarial network
nodes.definition: A generator network trained against a discriminator network until the generator produces samples the discriminator cannot tell from real data.

nodes.name: combinatorial explosion
nodes.slide: Solving Puzzles: How Big Is the Search?
nodes.label: Combinatorial explosion
nodes.definition: The rapid growth in the number of possible states or configurations, which makes exhaustive search impossible and forces learning structure instead.

nodes.name: correlation matrix
nodes.label: Correlation matrix
nodes.definition: The matrix of correlation coefficients between every pair of variables, with ones on the diagonal.

nodes.name: simpsons paradox
nodes.label: Simpson's paradox
nodes.definition: A trend that appears in pooled data reverses or disappears inside every subgroup, because a hidden grouping variable drives it.

nodes.name: box plot
nodes.label: Box plot
nodes.definition: A summary of a distribution by five numbers: minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum.

nodes.name: first principles model
nodes.slide: Recap: From Empirical Laws to Models
nodes.label: First-principles model
nodes.definition: A model derived from fundamental laws such as conservation and Newton's laws, rather than fitted to a chosen functional form.

nodes.name: inductive bias
nodes.label: Inductive bias
nodes.definition: The assumptions built into a model or learning method that let it generalise beyond the data it was trained on.

nodes.name: field
nodes.label: Field
nodes.definition: A quantity defined at every point in space and time, written u(x, t), such as temperature or velocity.

nodes.name: physical units
nodes.label: Physical units
nodes.definition: The dimensions attached to a quantity, such as meters or seconds, which carry its physical meaning and scale.

nodes.name: finite difference
nodes.label: Finite difference
nodes.definition: Approximating a derivative by the difference of function values at nearby points divided by their spacing.

nodes.name: differential equation
nodes.label: Differential equation
nodes.definition: An equation that relates an unknown function to its derivatives, describing how a quantity changes.

nodes.name: analytical solution
nodes.label: Analytical solution
nodes.definition: A closed-form formula that solves an equation exactly, obtained by hand rather than by computation.

nodes.name: ordinary differential equation
nodes.label: Ordinary differential equation
nodes.definition: A differential equation for a function of a single variable, usually time.

nodes.name: dynamical system
nodes.label: Dynamical system
nodes.definition: A system whose state changes over time according to a fixed rule, such as a differential equation.

nodes.name: conservation law
nodes.label: Conservation law
nodes.definition: A statement that a quantity is neither created nor destroyed, so its accumulation in a region equals flux in minus flux out.

nodes.name: flux
nodes.label: Flux
nodes.definition: The rate at which a quantity flows across a boundary per unit time.

nodes.name: continuity equation
nodes.label: Continuity equation
nodes.definition: The differential form of a conservation law: the time derivative of a density plus the divergence of its flux equals zero.

nodes.name: divergence
nodes.label: Divergence
nodes.definition: A measure of the net outflow of a vector field from a point, the sum of the partial derivatives of its components.

nodes.name: linearization
nodes.label: Linearization
nodes.definition: Approximating a nonlinear system by a linear one near an operating point or equilibrium.

nodes.name: navier stokes equations
nodes.label: Navier-Stokes equations
nodes.definition: The partial differential equations for momentum conservation in a viscous fluid, combining Newton's second law with the law of viscosity.

nodes.name: material derivative
nodes.label: Material derivative
nodes.definition: The rate of change of a quantity following a moving fluid particle, the local change plus the convective change.

nodes.name: turbulence
nodes.label: Turbulence
nodes.definition: Irregular, multi-scale fluid motion produced by the nonlinear convective term of the Navier-Stokes equations.

nodes.name: partial differential equation
nodes.label: Partial differential equation
nodes.definition: An equation relating a function of several variables, such as space and time, to its partial derivatives.

nodes.name: advection equation
nodes.label: Advection equation
nodes.definition: A first-order PDE whose solution is the initial profile transported at constant speed without changing shape.

nodes.name: diffusion equation
nodes.label: Diffusion equation
nodes.definition: A PDE in which a quantity changes at a rate proportional to its curvature, so peaks flatten and the profile spreads out.

nodes.name: wave equation
nodes.label: Wave equation
nodes.definition: A second-order PDE whose solutions are disturbances that propagate at a fixed speed in both directions.

nodes.name: advection diffusion equation
nodes.label: Advection-diffusion equation
nodes.definition: A PDE combining transport at a speed with spreading by diffusion, as for a pollutant carried down a river.

nodes.name: reaction diffusion equation
nodes.label: Reaction-diffusion equation
nodes.definition: A diffusion equation with a local, often nonlinear, reaction or growth term added.

nodes.name: pattern formation
nodes.label: Pattern formation
nodes.definition: The spontaneous emergence of spatial structures such as spots and stripes from nonlinear local interactions plus diffusion.

nodes.name: damped oscillator
nodes.label: Damped oscillator
nodes.definition: A second-order system, like an RLC circuit or a spring with friction, that oscillates while its amplitude decays.

nodes.name: inverse problem
nodes.label: Inverse problem
nodes.definition: Inferring the causes or parameters of a system, such as a circuit, from observations of its output.

nodes.name: dimensional analysis
nodes.label: Dimensional analysis
nodes.definition: Using the units of quantities to check equations, derive relationships, and identify which terms dominate at a given scale.

nodes.name: autoregressive model
nodes.label: Autoregressive model
nodes.definition: A model that generates a sequence by feeding each output back in as the next input, as in time stepping or next-word prediction.

nodes.name: initial value problem
nodes.label: Initial value problem
nodes.definition: A differential equation together with the state at a starting time, from which the future trajectory is determined.

nodes.name: modeling assumption
nodes.label: Modeling assumption
nodes.definition: A simplification built into a model, such as linear response or a continuous medium, whose violation explains when the model fails.

nodes.name: recursion
nodes.label: Recursion
nodes.definition: Generating results by applying a rule repeatedly, each output becoming the next input.

nodes.name: recurrence relation
nodes.label: Recurrence relation
nodes.definition: An equation that defines each term of a sequence from previous terms, like the Fibonacci rule.

nodes.name: cellular automaton
nodes.label: Cellular automaton
nodes.definition: A grid of cells updated in discrete steps by a local rule that depends only on each cell's neighbours.

nodes.name: emergence
nodes.label: Emergence
nodes.definition: Complex global behaviour arising from simple local rules, as in the Game of Life.

nodes.name: discretization
nodes.label: Discretization
nodes.definition: Replacing continuous derivatives with differences on a grid so a differential equation becomes an algebraic update a computer can run.

nodes.name: euler method
nodes.label: Euler method
nodes.definition: The simplest time-stepping scheme: advance the state by the current derivative times the time step.

nodes.name: time step
nodes.label: Time step
nodes.definition: The interval between successive updates in a numerical simulation, trading accuracy and stability against speed.

nodes.name: lotka volterra model
nodes.label: Lotka-Volterra model
nodes.definition: A pair of nonlinear ODEs for predator and prey populations whose interaction produces sustained oscillations.

nodes.name: parameter estimation
nodes.label: Parameter estimation
nodes.definition: Choosing the constants of a model so its simulated output matches observed data.

nodes.name: pendulum
nodes.label: Pendulum
nodes.definition: A mass on a rod whose angle obeys a nonlinear second-order ODE, harmonic only for small swings.

nodes.name: phase space
nodes.label: Phase space
nodes.definition: The space of all states of a dynamical system, such as angle and angular velocity, in which a trajectory is a curve.

nodes.name: truncation error
nodes.label: Truncation error
nodes.definition: The error a numerical scheme makes by dropping the higher-order terms of a Taylor expansion.

nodes.name: taylor expansion
nodes.label: Taylor expansion
nodes.definition: Writing a function near a point as a polynomial built from its derivatives at that point.

nodes.name: order of accuracy
nodes.label: Order of accuracy
nodes.definition: How fast a scheme's error shrinks as the step size shrinks, for example proportional to the step or to its square.

nodes.name: computational grid
nodes.label: Computational grid
nodes.definition: The set of discrete points in space and time at which a numerical solution is computed.

nodes.name: stencil
nodes.label: Stencil
nodes.definition: The pattern of neighbouring grid points a finite-difference update uses to compute a new value.

nodes.name: explicit vs implicit scheme
nodes.label: Explicit and implicit schemes
nodes.definition: Explicit schemes compute the next state directly from the current one; implicit schemes solve a linear system and are more stable.

nodes.name: crank nicolson
nodes.label: Crank-Nicolson method
nodes.definition: An implicit scheme that averages forward and backward time steps, second-order accurate in time and space.

nodes.name: numerical stability
nodes.label: Numerical stability
nodes.definition: Whether errors in a numerical scheme stay bounded or blow up as the computation proceeds.

nodes.name: cfl condition
nodes.label: CFL condition
nodes.definition: The Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy limit on the time step relative to the grid spacing, beyond which an explicit scheme becomes unstable.

nodes.name: runge kutta
nodes.label: Runge-Kutta method
nodes.definition: A family of time-stepping schemes that sample the slope at several points within a step; RK4 is fourth-order accurate.

nodes.name: adaptive time stepping
nodes.label: Adaptive time stepping
nodes.definition: Automatically adjusting the time step during a simulation based on an estimate of the local error.

nodes.name: finite volume method
nodes.label: Finite volume method
nodes.definition: A discretization that tracks fluxes between cells so that conserved quantities are preserved exactly.

nodes.name: upwind scheme
nodes.label: Upwind scheme
nodes.definition: A discretization that takes flux values from the side the flow is coming from, so information travels in the right direction.

nodes.name: operator splitting
nodes.label: Operator splitting
nodes.definition: Solving a complicated equation by applying its parts, such as diffusion and advection, one after another in each time step.

nodes.name: semi lagrangian advection
nodes.label: Semi-Lagrangian advection
nodes.definition: Advecting a quantity by tracing each grid point backward along the velocity to find where its value came from.

nodes.name: pressure projection
nodes.label: Pressure projection
nodes.definition: Making a velocity field divergence-free by solving a Poisson equation for pressure and subtracting its gradient.

nodes.name: rayleigh benard convection
nodes.label: Rayleigh-Benard convection
nodes.definition: Convection in a fluid heated from below and cooled from above, which forms rolling cells and drives weather.

nodes.name: model reduction
nodes.slide: From 7 Equations to 3: The Saltzman-Lorenz Story
nodes.label: Model reduction
nodes.definition: Replacing a large model with a smaller one that keeps only the variables that drive the dynamics.

nodes.name: lorenz system
nodes.label: Lorenz system
nodes.definition: Three coupled nonlinear ODEs reduced from a convection model, the classic example of deterministic chaos.

nodes.name: strange attractor
nodes.label: Strange attractor
nodes.definition: A fractal set in phase space that chaotic trajectories approach and wander on without ever repeating.

nodes.name: sensitivity to initial conditions
nodes.label: Sensitivity to initial conditions
nodes.definition: The property that arbitrarily small differences in starting state grow until trajectories diverge completely.

nodes.name: chaos
nodes.label: Chaos
nodes.definition: Deterministic dynamics in which tiny differences in initial conditions grow exponentially, making long-term prediction impossible.

nodes.name: complex system
nodes.label: Complex system
nodes.definition: A system of many interacting parts whose collective behavior cannot be understood by studying the parts one at a time.

nodes.name: ensemble
nodes.label: Ensemble
nodes.definition: A collection of simulations started from slightly different initial conditions, used to represent uncertainty as a distribution.

nodes.name: probability mass function
nodes.label: Probability mass function
nodes.definition: A function giving the probability that a discrete random variable takes each of its possible values.

nodes.name: kernel density estimation
nodes.label: Kernel density estimation
nodes.definition: Estimating a probability density by placing a small smooth bump on each sample and summing them.

nodes.name: random variable
nodes.label: Random variable
nodes.definition: A function that assigns a number to each outcome of a random experiment.

nodes.name: expectation
nodes.label: Expectation
nodes.definition: The probability-weighted average value of a random variable, its center of mass.

nodes.name: variance
nodes.label: Variance
nodes.definition: The expected squared distance of a random variable from its mean, a measure of spread.

nodes.name: joint probability
nodes.label: Joint probability
nodes.definition: The probability that two or more events or random variables take given values at the same time.

nodes.name: conditional probability
nodes.label: Conditional probability
nodes.definition: The probability of one event given that another event is known to have happened.

nodes.name: independence
nodes.label: Independence
nodes.definition: Two random variables are independent when knowing one tells you nothing about the other, so their joint probability factorizes.

nodes.name: central limit theorem
nodes.label: Central limit theorem
nodes.definition: The average of many independent random variables with finite variance tends toward a Gaussian distribution.

nodes.name: brownian motion
nodes.label: Brownian motion
nodes.definition: The erratic movement of a small particle pushed by random molecular collisions, the physical model of continuous random motion.

nodes.name: random walk
nodes.label: Random walk
nodes.definition: A process that moves by a random step at each time, the discrete model of diffusion.

nodes.name: master equation
nodes.label: Master equation
nodes.definition: An equation for how the probability of each state changes in time from the rates of jumping between states.

nodes.name: continuum limit
nodes.label: Continuum limit
nodes.definition: Letting grid spacing and time step shrink to zero so a discrete update rule becomes a differential equation.

nodes.name: stochastic differential equation
nodes.slide: What if $\Delta x \to 0$? Random $dx$ at every $dt$?
nodes.label: Stochastic differential equation
nodes.definition: A differential equation with a random forcing term, describing individual noisy trajectories.

nodes.name: coarse graining
nodes.label: Coarse-graining
nodes.definition: Describing a system at a larger scale by averaging over fine details, which can turn random microscopic behavior into predictable macroscopic laws.

nodes.name: network
nodes.label: Network
nodes.definition: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to represent systems whose parts interact along specific links.

nodes.name: fitzhugh nagumo model
nodes.label: FitzHugh-Nagumo model
nodes.definition: A two-variable simplification of neuron dynamics that produces spiking and oscillation.

nodes.name: coupled oscillators
nodes.label: Coupled oscillators
nodes.definition: Several oscillating units that influence each other through connections such as springs or synapses.

nodes.name: synchronization
nodes.label: Synchronization
nodes.definition: The tendency of coupled oscillators to lock into a common rhythm when coupling is strong enough.

nodes.name: stationarity
nodes.slide: First Rule: LOOK at the Data
nodes.label: Stationarity
nodes.definition: The property that a time series' statistics such as mean and variance do not change over time.

nodes.name: fourier series
nodes.label: Fourier series
nodes.definition: Representing a signal as a weighted sum of sines and cosines at different frequencies.

nodes.name: seasonality
nodes.slide: What Is Left Is the Weather
nodes.label: Seasonality
nodes.definition: A repeating pattern in a time series tied to a calendar period such as a year or a day.

nodes.name: short time fourier transform
nodes.label: Short-time Fourier transform
nodes.definition: Computing the Fourier transform over a sliding window to see how frequency content changes over time.

nodes.name: basis function
nodes.label: Basis function
nodes.definition: One member of a chosen set of functions, such as sines, polynomials or wavelets, whose weighted sum represents a signal.

nodes.name: separation of variables
nodes.label: Separation of variables
nodes.definition: Solving a partial differential equation by assuming the solution is a product of functions of each variable separately.

nodes.name: normal mode
nodes.label: Normal mode
nodes.definition: A pattern of motion in which all parts of a linear system oscillate at the same single frequency.

nodes.name: fermi pasta ulam tsingou problem
nodes.label: Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou problem
nodes.definition: A 1953 simulation of a nonlinear spring chain in which energy unexpectedly returned to its initial mode instead of spreading out.

nodes.name: arima
nodes.label: ARIMA
nodes.definition: An extension of autoregressive models that adds differencing to remove trends and moving-average terms on past errors.

nodes.name: nonlinear autoregressive model
nodes.label: Nonlinear autoregressive model
nodes.definition: An autoregressive model whose features include nonlinear functions of past values, such as their squares and products.

nodes.name: logistic map
nodes.label: Logistic map
nodes.definition: The discrete population model x next equals r x (1 minus x), which shows period doubling and chaos as r grows.

nodes.name: system identification
nodes.label: System identification
nodes.definition: Estimating the parameters of a dynamical model from measured input and output data.

nodes.name: numerical differentiation
nodes.label: Numerical differentiation
nodes.definition: Estimating derivatives from sampled data, a step that amplifies noise.

nodes.name: feature library
nodes.label: Feature library
nodes.definition: A set of candidate functions of the state from which a sparse model selects the terms of an equation.

nodes.name: dimensionality reduction
nodes.label: Dimensionality reduction
nodes.definition: Representing high-dimensional data with fewer variables while keeping most of its structure.

nodes.name: curse of dimensionality
nodes.label: Curse of dimensionality
nodes.definition: As the number of dimensions grows, data becomes sparse and models need exponentially more samples.

nodes.name: principal component analysis
nodes.label: Principal component analysis
nodes.definition: Finding orthogonal directions of maximum variance in data and projecting onto the top few.

nodes.name: standardization
nodes.label: Standardization
nodes.definition: Rescaling each feature to zero mean and unit standard deviation so features are comparable.

nodes.name: reconstruction error
nodes.label: Reconstruction error
nodes.definition: The distance between original data and its approximation after projecting to fewer dimensions and back.

nodes.name: lagrange multiplier
nodes.label: Lagrange multiplier
nodes.definition: A variable added to turn a constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one.

nodes.name: explained variance
nodes.label: Explained variance
nodes.definition: The fraction of total variance in the data captured by a given set of principal components.

nodes.name: singular value decomposition
nodes.label: Singular value decomposition
nodes.definition: Factoring any matrix as U times Sigma times V transpose, with orthogonal U and V and nonnegative singular values.

nodes.name: low rank approximation
nodes.label: Low-rank approximation
nodes.definition: Approximating a matrix by keeping only its largest singular values and their vectors.

nodes.name: eigenfaces
nodes.slide: Eigenfaces: Faces as Points in High-D Space
nodes.label: Eigenfaces
nodes.definition: Principal components of a set of face images, used as a basis to represent and reconstruct faces.

nodes.name: scree plot
nodes.label: Scree plot
nodes.definition: A plot of singular values or eigenvalues in decreasing order used to choose how many components to keep.

nodes.name: linear dynamical system
nodes.label: Linear dynamical system
nodes.definition: A system whose rate of change is a constant matrix times its state.

nodes.name: eigendecomposition
nodes.label: Eigendecomposition
nodes.definition: Writing a square matrix as V Lambda V inverse, with eigenvectors in V and eigenvalues on the diagonal of Lambda.

nodes.name: modal decoupling
nodes.label: Modal decoupling
nodes.definition: Changing to eigenvector coordinates so a coupled linear system becomes independent one-dimensional equations.

nodes.name: linear stability
nodes.label: Linear stability
nodes.definition: How eigenvalues of a linear system determine whether solutions grow, decay or oscillate.

nodes.name: vortex shedding
nodes.label: Vortex shedding
nodes.definition: The periodic release of alternating vortices behind an obstacle in a flow.

nodes.name: snapshot matrix
nodes.label: Snapshot matrix
nodes.definition: A data matrix whose columns are the system's full state measured at successive times.

nodes.name: proper orthogonal decomposition
nodes.label: Proper orthogonal decomposition
nodes.definition: Applying SVD to a snapshot matrix to get energy-ranked spatial modes of a field.

nodes.name: pseudo inverse
nodes.label: Pseudo-inverse
nodes.definition: A generalized inverse of a rectangular matrix that gives the least-squares solution of a linear system.

nodes.name: dynamic mode decomposition
nodes.label: Dynamic mode decomposition
nodes.definition: Fitting a best linear map between successive snapshots and decomposing it into spatial modes each with one growth rate and frequency.

nodes.name: koopman operator
nodes.label: Koopman operator
nodes.definition: A linear operator that advances functions of the state of a nonlinear system, making nonlinear dynamics linear in a larger space.

nodes.name: savitzky golay filter
nodes.label: Savitzky-Golay filter
nodes.definition: Smoothing and differentiating data by fitting a low-degree polynomial in a sliding window.

nodes.name: sparse regression
nodes.label: Sparse regression
nodes.definition: Regression that forces most coefficients to be exactly zero so only a few terms remain.

nodes.name: sequential thresholded least squares
nodes.label: Sequential thresholded least squares
nodes.definition: Repeatedly solving least squares and zeroing coefficients below a threshold until the active set stops changing.

nodes.name: sindy
nodes.label: SINDy
nodes.definition: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics: discovering a governing equation by sparse regression over a library of candidate terms.

nodes.name: pde discovery
nodes.label: PDE discovery
nodes.definition: Extending sparse regression to libraries of spatial derivatives to learn partial differential equations from data on a grid.

nodes.name: self organization
nodes.label: Self-Organization
nodes.definition: Global order or capability emerging from many simple elements that adapt and coordinate locally, without a central designer.

nodes.name: rule based system
nodes.slide: Rules vs. the Ability to Learn
nodes.label: Rule-Based System
nodes.definition: A program that acts by following explicit rules written by experts, rather than learning its behaviour from data.

nodes.name: voltage clamp
nodes.slide: From Theory to Biology: The Squid Giant Axon
nodes.label: Voltage Clamp
nodes.definition: An experimental technique that holds a neuron's membrane voltage fixed so the ionic currents through it can be measured.

nodes.name: hodgkin huxley model
nodes.label: Hodgkin-Huxley Model
nodes.definition: A set of coupled differential equations, fitted to squid axon data, that describes how ion channels produce a neuron's spike.

nodes.name: representation learning
nodes.label: Representation Learning
nodes.definition: Letting a model learn its own features from raw data, with deeper layers building more abstract features from simpler ones.

nodes.name: adam optimizer
nodes.label: Adam Optimizer
nodes.definition: A gradient-based optimizer that adapts the step size of each parameter using running averages of its gradients and squared gradients.

nodes.name: pytorch
nodes.label: PyTorch
nodes.definition: A Python library for building and training neural networks, with tensors, layers, optimizers and automatic differentiation.

nodes.name: dropout
nodes.label: Dropout
nodes.definition: A regularization technique that randomly switches off neurons during training so the network cannot rely on any single unit.

nodes.name: early stopping
nodes.label: Early Stopping
nodes.definition: Halting training when the validation loss stops improving, to avoid overfitting the training data.

nodes.name: ising model
nodes.label: Ising Model
nodes.definition: A statistical mechanics model of a grid of up-or-down spins whose neighbours prefer to align, used to study magnetism and phase transitions.

nodes.name: metropolis hastings
nodes.label: Metropolis-Hastings Algorithm
nodes.definition: A sampling method that proposes random changes and accepts them with a probability set by the change in energy or likelihood.

nodes.name: hopfield network
nodes.slide: From Spins to Neurons: Hopfield Networks (1982)
nodes.label: Hopfield Network
nodes.definition: A fully connected network of binary neurons with symmetric weights whose energy minima store patterns as memories.

nodes.name: energy based model
nodes.slide: From Spins to Neurons: Hopfield Networks (1982)
nodes.label: Energy-Based Model
nodes.definition: A model that assigns an energy to every configuration so that likely or desired configurations have low energy.

nodes.name: associative memory
nodes.label: Associative Memory
nodes.definition: A memory that retrieves a complete stored pattern from a partial or corrupted version of it.

nodes.name: attention
nodes.label: Attention
nodes.definition: A mechanism that combines stored values weighted by the softmax similarity between a query and a set of keys.

nodes.name: boltzmann machine
nodes.label: Boltzmann Machine
nodes.definition: A stochastic network of visible and hidden binary units whose joint probability follows a Boltzmann distribution over an energy function.

nodes.name: boltzmann distribution
nodes.label: Boltzmann Distribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution in which a configuration's probability decays exponentially with its energy divided by temperature.

nodes.name: hidden state
nodes.label: Hidden State
nodes.definition: An internal vector a sequence model updates at each time step to carry information about the past.

nodes.name: state space model
nodes.label: State-Space Model
nodes.definition: A model in which a hidden state evolves by an update rule driven by inputs, and observations are read out from that state.

nodes.name: backpropagation through time
nodes.label: Backpropagation Through Time
nodes.definition: Training a recurrent network by unrolling it over the sequence and applying backpropagation through every time step.

nodes.name: vanishing gradient
nodes.label: Vanishing Gradient
nodes.definition: The shrinking of gradients as they are multiplied back through many layers or time steps, which stops early parts of a network from learning.

nodes.name: spectral radius
nodes.label: Spectral Radius
nodes.definition: The largest absolute value among a matrix's eigenvalues, which sets whether repeated multiplication by it grows or shrinks vectors.

nodes.name: lstm
nodes.label: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
nodes.definition: A recurrent network whose gates control what a cell state forgets, stores and outputs, letting it keep information over long sequences.

nodes.name: reservoir computing
nodes.label: Reservoir Computing
nodes.definition: Using a fixed, randomly connected recurrent network as a dynamical reservoir and training only a linear readout from its states.

nodes.name: echo state property
nodes.label: Echo State Property
nodes.definition: The requirement that a reservoir's state depends on its input history and forgets its initial condition over time.

nodes.name: physical reservoir computing
nodes.label: Physical Reservoir Computing
nodes.definition: Using a real physical system with nonlinear, fading-memory dynamics, such as optics or mechanics, as the reservoir of a reservoir computer.

nodes.name: kuramoto sivashinsky equation
nodes.label: Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Equation
nodes.definition: A fourth-order nonlinear PDE from flame fronts and chemical oscillations that is a standard test case for spatiotemporal chaos.

nodes.name: spatiotemporal chaos
nodes.label: Spatiotemporal Chaos
nodes.definition: Chaotic behaviour that is irregular in both space and time, with sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

nodes.name: lyapunov time
nodes.label: Lyapunov Time
nodes.definition: The characteristic time over which small errors in a chaotic system grow by a factor of e, setting the horizon of useful prediction.

nodes.name: symbolic regression
nodes.label: Symbolic regression
nodes.definition: Searching over mathematical expressions to find a formula that fits data, without fixing the candidate terms in advance.

nodes.name: expression tree
nodes.label: Expression Tree
nodes.definition: A tree representation of a formula in which internal nodes are operators and leaves are variables or constants.

nodes.name: genetic programming
nodes.label: Genetic Programming
nodes.definition: An evolutionary search that improves a population of programs or expression trees through selection, crossover and mutation.

nodes.name: fitness function
nodes.label: Fitness Function
nodes.definition: The score an evolutionary algorithm uses to rank candidates, often fit error plus a penalty for complexity.

nodes.name: selection
nodes.label: Selection
nodes.definition: The step of an evolutionary algorithm that chooses which candidates reproduce, favouring those with better fitness.

nodes.name: crossover
nodes.label: Crossover
nodes.definition: Creating offspring in an evolutionary algorithm by combining parts of two parents, such as swapping subtrees.

nodes.name: mutation
nodes.label: Mutation
nodes.definition: A random change to a candidate in an evolutionary algorithm, which introduces new material into the population.

nodes.name: keplers third law
nodes.slide: Now Do It On Something Real
nodes.label: Kepler's Third Law
nodes.definition: The law that a planet's orbital period squared is proportional to its orbital distance cubed, divided by the star's mass.

nodes.name: power law
nodes.slide: A Straight Line Where You Did Not Expect One
nodes.label: Power Law
nodes.definition: A relationship of the form y = C x^a, which appears as a straight line on a log-log plot.

nodes.name: pareto front
nodes.label: Pareto Front
nodes.definition: The set of candidates that no other candidate beats on every objective at once, such as accuracy and simplicity.

nodes.name: pysr
nodes.label: PySR
nodes.definition: A high-performance open-source library for symbolic regression using parallel evolving populations.

nodes.name: bloat
nodes.label: Bloat
nodes.definition: The tendency of evolved expression trees to grow larger without improving their fitness.

nodes.name: boundary condition
nodes.slide: The Problem We Want to Solve
nodes.label: Boundary Condition
nodes.definition: A constraint on a differential equation's solution at the edges of its domain or at the initial time.

nodes.name: basis expansion
nodes.label: Basis Expansion
nodes.definition: Writing an unknown function as a weighted sum of fixed known functions such as sines or polynomials.

nodes.name: pde residual
nodes.label: PDE Residual
nodes.definition: What remains when a candidate solution is substituted into a differential equation; it is zero everywhere for an exact solution.

nodes.name: collocation method
nodes.label: Collocation Method
nodes.definition: Finding an approximate solution of a differential equation by making its residual small at a chosen set of points.

nodes.name: physics informed neural network
nodes.slide: The PINN: Neural Network as Solution
nodes.label: Physics-informed neural network
nodes.definition: A neural network trained so that its output satisfies a differential equation, by adding the equation residual to the loss.

nodes.name: automatic differentiation
nodes.label: Automatic Differentiation
nodes.definition: Computing exact derivatives of a program by applying the chain rule through its computation graph.

nodes.name: physics informed loss
nodes.label: Physics-Informed Loss
nodes.definition: A loss that adds weighted terms for data fit, PDE residual and boundary conditions so one optimisation respects both data and physics.

nodes.name: mesh free method
nodes.label: Mesh-Free Method
nodes.definition: A numerical method that evaluates the solution at scattered points without building a mesh or grid.

nodes.name: forward problem
nodes.slide: Forward Problem: Solving a Known PDE
nodes.label: Forward Problem
nodes.definition: Computing a system's solution when the governing equation and all its parameters are known.

nodes.name: loss balancing
nodes.label: Loss Balancing
nodes.definition: Choosing or adapting the weights of different loss terms so that none dominates training.

nodes.name: spectral bias
nodes.label: Spectral Bias
nodes.definition: The tendency of neural networks to learn low-frequency components of a function before high-frequency ones.

nodes.name: fourier features
nodes.label: Fourier Features
nodes.definition: Mapping inputs through sines and cosines of random frequencies before a network so it can represent high-frequency detail.

nodes.name: operator
nodes.label: Operator
nodes.definition: A map that takes a function as input and returns another function.

nodes.name: discretization invariance
nodes.label: Discretization Invariance
nodes.definition: The property that a learned model works on input and output grids of any resolution without retraining.

nodes.name: operator universal approximation
nodes.label: Universal Approximation for Operators
nodes.definition: The theorem that a suitable neural network can approximate any continuous nonlinear operator between function spaces.

nodes.name: neural operator
nodes.label: Neural Operator
nodes.definition: A neural network that maps whole input functions to output functions, such as initial conditions to PDE solutions.

nodes.name: solution operator
nodes.label: Solution Operator
nodes.definition: The map that takes a PDE's input data, such as an initial condition or forcing, to its solution.

nodes.name: modal decomposition
nodes.label: Modal Decomposition
nodes.definition: Writing a field as a sum of spatial modes weighted by time-dependent coefficients.

nodes.name: deeponet
nodes.label: DeepONet
nodes.definition: A neural operator that combines a branch network encoding the input function with a trunk network encoding the query point by a dot product.

nodes.name: greens function
nodes.label: Green's Function
nodes.definition: The response of a linear differential equation to a point impulse, from which any solution is built by integrating against the forcing.

nodes.name: integral kernel layer
nodes.slide: From Green's Functions to Neural Operator Layers
nodes.label: Integral Kernel Layer
nodes.definition: A neural network layer that transforms a function by integrating it against a learned kernel, generalising a weight matrix to functions.

nodes.name: fourier neural operator
nodes.label: Fourier Neural Operator
nodes.definition: A neural operator whose layers multiply learned weights on a truncated set of Fourier modes, acting as a learned global convolution.

nodes.name: self supervised learning
nodes.label: Self-Supervised Learning
nodes.definition: Learning from unlabeled data by predicting part of the data from other parts, so the data supplies its own labels.

nodes.name: next token prediction
nodes.label: Next-Token Prediction
nodes.definition: The training objective of predicting each token in a sequence from the tokens before it.

nodes.name: pretraining
nodes.label: Pretraining
nodes.definition: The first, large-scale training stage of a model on broad unlabeled data before it is adapted to specific tasks.

nodes.name: foundation model
nodes.label: Foundation Model
nodes.definition: A large model pretrained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks.

nodes.name: transformer
nodes.label: Transformer
nodes.definition: A neural network architecture built from stacked attention layers that processes a whole sequence at once rather than step by step.

nodes.name: scaling law
nodes.label: Scaling Law
nodes.definition: An empirical power-law relation showing how model loss falls as compute, data, or parameters grow.

nodes.name: fine tuning
nodes.slide: Adaptation: From Raw Model to Useful Assistant
nodes.label: Fine-Tuning
nodes.definition: Continuing to train a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset to adapt its behavior.

nodes.name: rlhf
nodes.slide: Adaptation: From Raw Model to Useful Assistant
nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
nodes.definition: Adapting a language model with a reward model learned from human preference judgments.

nodes.name: in context learning
nodes.slide: Adaptation: From Raw Model to Useful Assistant
nodes.label: In-Context Learning
nodes.definition: A model adapting to a task from examples given in its prompt, without any weight updates.

nodes.name: emergent capability
nodes.label: Emergent Capability
nodes.definition: An ability that appears in large models but seems absent in smaller ones, sometimes argued to be a measurement artifact.

nodes.name: protein structure prediction
nodes.label: Protein Structure Prediction
nodes.definition: Predicting the 3D folded shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence, as done by AlphaFold.

nodes.name: protein language model
nodes.label: Protein Language Model
nodes.definition: A language model trained on protein sequences, treating amino acids as tokens, used to predict or design proteins.

nodes.name: ai weather forecasting
nodes.label: AI Weather Forecasting
nodes.definition: Learned models such as GraphCast and GenCast that predict global weather from reanalysis data, rivaling numerical forecasts.

nodes.name: evolutionary search
nodes.label: Evolutionary Search
nodes.definition: An optimization loop that proposes candidates, scores them with an evaluator, and keeps and mutates the best ones.

nodes.name: ai agent
nodes.label: AI Agent
nodes.definition: A system in which a language model plans, chooses tools, executes actions, and iterates toward a goal using memory.

nodes.name: tool use
nodes.label: Tool Use
nodes.definition: A language model calling external functions such as code, search, or simulators through structured descriptions of their inputs.

nodes.name: react loop
nodes.label: ReAct Loop
nodes.definition: An agent loop that interleaves reasoning steps with actions and observations until a task is done.

nodes.name: coding agent
nodes.slide: Inside a Real Agent: Claude Code
nodes.label: Coding Agent
nodes.definition: An AI agent whose tools read, edit, search, and run code in a software project.

nodes.name: prompt engineering
nodes.label: Prompt Engineering
nodes.definition: Designing the instructions, tools, and constraints given to a language model to shape its behavior.

nodes.name: science agent
nodes.label: Science Agent
nodes.definition: An AI agent whose tools are scientific operations such as data analysis, simulation, literature search, and lab experiments.

nodes.name: autonomous discovery
nodes.label: Autonomous Discovery
nodes.definition: Scientific discovery in which AI systems generate hypotheses, design and run experiments, and analyze results with little human input.

nodes.name: multi agent system
nodes.label: Multi-Agent System
nodes.definition: A system in which several AI agents with different roles cooperate on a task.

nodes.name: scientific method
nodes.label: Scientific Method
nodes.definition: The cycle of observing, hypothesizing, experimenting, analyzing, and revising that produces scientific knowledge.

nodes.name: hallucination
nodes.label: Hallucination
nodes.definition: A language model producing fluent, confident output that is factually false or fabricated.

nodes.name: mechanistic interpretability
nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.definition: Studying a trained network's internal representations and circuits to explain how they cause its behavior.

nodes.name: reward hacking
nodes.label: Reward Hacking
nodes.definition: A model maximizing its training or evaluation signal in unintended ways that defeat the actual goal.

nodes.name: research taste
nodes.label: Research Taste
nodes.definition: The judgment to recognize which questions matter and which results are meaningful, built through repeated iteration.

nodes.name: engineering responsibility
nodes.label: Engineering Responsibility
nodes.definition: An engineer's awareness of where their work sits in a chain of tools and ends, and of the purposes it ultimately serves.

nodes.name: ai unpredictability
nodes.label: AI Unpredictability
nodes.definition: The fact that capable AI systems behave and get used in ways their builders cannot fully foresee, traded off against their usefulness.

nodes.name: consequence distribution
nodes.label: Consequence Distribution
nodes.definition: Viewing a tool's outcomes as a probability distribution over good and bad effects, to be shifted and narrowed.

nodes.name: ai safety
nodes.label: AI Safety
nodes.definition: Practices and standards for managing the risks of AI systems, analogous to warning labels and clinical trials for other technologies.

nodes.name: human centered testing
nodes.label: Human-Centered Testing
nodes.definition: Releasing a tool by prototyping, watching real users, documenting failures, and writing guidance before wide release.

nodes.name: applied ethics
nodes.label: Applied Ethics
nodes.definition: Ethical reasoning about whether a specific action or technology is good or bad.

nodes.name: normative ethics
nodes.label: Normative Ethics
nodes.definition: Theories such as utilitarianism, deontology, and virtue ethics that say what should govern moral judgments.

nodes.name: meta ethics
nodes.label: Meta-Ethics
nodes.definition: The study of whether moral facts exist and what moral claims mean.

nodes.name: epistemic humility
nodes.label: Epistemic Humility
nodes.definition: Acknowledging that one's knowledge rests on assumptions that can fail and actively inspecting them.

nodes.name: bias to action
nodes.label: Bias to Action
nodes.definition: Acting on a best current hypothesis and learning from feedback rather than waiting for certainty.

nodes.name: problem formulation
nodes.label: Problem Formulation
nodes.definition: Defining what problem to solve and how to frame it, a skill prior to choosing any method.

questions.question: Who wrote the twelve disputed Federalist Papers?
